quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, it is important to:

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Know what is happening both in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening both in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: You need to be aware of the road ahead. But you also cannot ignore what is behind you. Check your mirrors regularly to see what is happening behind you.

questions.question: When riding, your feet should be:
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding. This helps you stay balanced.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, you should care most about:
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Unlike other beverages, alcohol:

options.text: Goes into the bloodstream right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goes into the bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested like other foods and drinks. It passes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream and quickly reaches the brain.

questions.question: When cars are merging from an entrance ramp:

options.text: A motorcyclist should assume the entering drivers see them.
A motorcyclist should never assume the entering drivers see them.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should never assume the entering drivers see them.
questions.explanation: Do not assume merging drivers see you. Give them plenty of space. Change lanes away from them if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: When nearing a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume that other drivers will properly yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers when approaching a blind intersection.

questions.question: To work properly, eye or face shield protection must:

options.text: Limit your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear views to the sides, fasten securely, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Before riding, a motorcycle operator should check the throttle. The throttle should:
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when you release it, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train has passed and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect your body?

options.text: About one hour after drinking it.
About two hours after drinking it.

questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested to enter your bloodstream. It reaches your brain and affects your body within minutes of drinking it.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, what should you check?

options.text: It has no cracks or defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and be free of defects like cracks, loose padding, and frayed straps.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
No, they do not have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, should you wear a jacket?

options.text: Only wear one when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even in warm weather.

questions.question: What can happen if you lock your brakes?
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and reapply it. If your rear brake locks on a surface with good traction, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: How can you lower the chances of a crash?

options.text: Assume other drivers will avoid hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible, clearly communicate your intentions, keep a safe distance, look ahead, identify hazards, and be ready to react to other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane to see better.
Ride close to the vehicle ahead to use their headlights.
Reduce your speed to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed to avoid unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: At night, ride slower than you would during the day. This gives you a better chance to avoid hazards. Also increase your following distance and be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: What material should a protective motorcycle jacket be made of?
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket that covers your arms completely and fits snugly. Leather or sturdy synthetic materials with body armor provide the best protection.

questions.question: How should you handle a tailgater?
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: If a rider wears a helmet during a crash, are they more likely to survive?

options.text: No, they are less likely to survive.
No, they have the same chance as someone without a helmet.
Yes, they are more likely to survive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are more likely to survive.
questions.explanation: Riders not wearing helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets during a crash.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time?

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is the best way.
Just start riding. Most bikes are similar, so you don't need to check safety features.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, check its safety and maintenance. Find where all controls are. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to understand how it works.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speed increases, what should you do?
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speed increases, you must shift into higher gears.

questions.question: What about footrests on a motorcycle?

options.text: The driver and passenger can share them.
They are required for both the driver and passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required for both the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Proper footing prevents your passenger from falling and pulling you off too.

questions.question: How can you become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: The only way to sober up is to give your body time to remove the alcohol. No tricks or methods can speed this up.

questions.question: What is the best way to make sure other drivers see your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Most motorcycles sold in the United States after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically when running. Check that your headlight works before every ride.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
Clothing that does not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you if you crash. It also keeps you comfortable and visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Hides you from other road users.
Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Keep safe space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: Which colors should motorcycle riders wear?
questions.explanation: Bright orange, red, yellow, and green are the best colors for riders to wear. These colors help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or similar durable material for maximum grip and protection.
